database_summary: Small web/app analytics schema with user master tables, many event/log tables (action/activity/read/form/access) and some product/category masters and sales/purchase facts. Logs are mostly event streams (many rows per session/user) while mst_ tables are descriptive. Some tables are historical snapshots (mst_products_YYYYMMDD). No declared PKs; relationships are implied by columns like user_id, session, product_id.

accepted.name: users_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id,
  sex,
  CASE WHEN length(trim(birth_date))>0 THEN date(birth_date) ELSE NULL END AS birth_date,
  CASE WHEN length(trim(register_date))>0 THEN date(register_date) ELSE NULL END AS register_date,
  register_device,
  CASE WHEN length(trim(withdraw_date))>0 THEN date(withdraw_date) ELSE NULL END AS withdraw_date,
  CASE
    WHEN length(trim(birth_date))>0 AND length(trim(register_date))>0
    THEN (strftime('%Y', date(register_date)) - strftime('%Y', date(birth_date)) - (strftime('%m-%d', date(register_date))<strftime('%m-%d', date(birth_date))))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS age_at_register
FROM mst_users
accepted.description: Normalized user master rows: canonical user_id with parsed date fields (birth_date, register_date, withdraw_date) converted to SQLite date() where possible and an age_at_register (years) derived when birth_date and register_date exist. Use this when joining user attributes to event logs or computing user cohorts by registration/age. | Use for: join users to event logs for user-level analysis; cohort users by register_date or age; filter active users (withdraw_date null) or compute time-to-withdrawal

accepted.name: users_with_contact
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.user_id AS user_id,
  m.sex AS sex,
  m.register_date AS register_date,
  a1.name AS name,
  a1.email AS email,
  a2.name AS name_app2,
  a2.phone AS phone,
  c.card_number AS card_number
FROM mst_users m
LEFT JOIN app1_mst_users a1 ON a1.user_id = m.user_id
LEFT JOIN app2_mst_users a2 ON a2.user_id = m.user_id
LEFT JOIN mst_users_with_card_number c ON c.user_id = m.user_id
accepted.description: Denormalized user contact information by left-joining application-specific user tables and card number table onto mst_users. Preserves original user_id and exposes optional name/email/phone/card_number. Use when resolving contact fields for a user across apps. | Use for: retrieve contact info for a user; count users with contact or card information; match event user_ids to contact attributes

accepted.name: event_actions_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  session,
  user_id,
  action,
  category,
  products,
  amount,
  CASE WHEN length(trim(stamp))>0 THEN datetime(stamp) ELSE NULL END AS stamp
FROM action_log
accepted.description: Cleaned action event stream: canonical stamp (as datetime), preserves session, user_id, action, category, products, amount. Useful as a standard input for event-level aggregation and joins. Does not filter out any rows. | Use for: aggregate actions by user or session; filter actions by time ranges; explode products field in downstream CTEs

accepted.name: purchases_by_user
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id,
  COUNT(*) AS purchase_count,
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount,
  MIN(CASE WHEN length(trim(stamp))>0 THEN datetime(stamp) ELSE NULL END) AS first_purchase_at,
  MAX(CASE WHEN length(trim(stamp))>0 THEN datetime(stamp) ELSE NULL END) AS last_purchase_at
FROM purchase_log
GROUP BY user_id
accepted.description: Aggregated purchase metrics per user: total_amount, purchase_count, first_purchase_at, last_purchase_at. Use for user monetization and lifetime value calculations. | Use for: compute LTV per user; join purchases to user attributes; identify active purchasers and recency

accepted.name: product_price_history_union
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT product_id, name, price, CASE WHEN length(trim(updated_at))>0 THEN datetime(updated_at) ELSE NULL END AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20161201
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id, name, price, CASE WHEN length(trim(updated_at))>0 THEN datetime(updated_at) ELSE NULL END AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20170101
accepted.description: Unioned product snapshots from dated product masters into a single product history relation with updated_at preserved. Use to compare product attributes across snapshots or to select latest product info. | Use for: track price changes over time; get latest product snapshot by product_id using a RANK CTE; join product historical attributes to event product references

accepted.name: latest_product_snapshot_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  name,
  price,
  updated_at,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS product_rank
FROM (
  SELECT product_id, name, price, CASE WHEN length(trim(updated_at))>0 THEN datetime(updated_at) ELSE NULL END AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20161201
  UNION ALL
  SELECT product_id, name, price, CASE WHEN length(trim(updated_at))>0 THEN datetime(updated_at) ELSE NULL END AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20170101
)
accepted.description: Per-product ranking of product snapshots ordered by updated_at desc; exposes product_rank so downstream queries can select the latest snapshot (WHERE product_rank = 1). Use to obtain the most recent product attributes across product snapshot tables. | Use for: retrieve latest product attributes; analyze price deltas between snapshots

accepted.name: product_sales_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  category_name,
  product_id,
  COALESCE(sales,0) AS sales
FROM product_sales
accepted.description: Normalized product sales rows: preserves category_name and product_id and ensures sales is numeric (0 when null). Use as base for top-product rankings or joining to product masters. | Use for: rank products by sales within category; join sales to product master data

accepted.name: top_products_by_category_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  category_name,
  product_id,
  sales,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_name ORDER BY sales DESC) AS category_rank
FROM (
  SELECT category_name, product_id, COALESCE(sales,0) AS sales FROM product_sales
)
accepted.description: Ranks products within each category by sales descending. Exposes category_rank so downstream queries can select top-N per category with a filter on category_rank. Useful for category-level merchandising and reporting. | Use for: select top-N products per category; compare category-leading products

accepted.name: session_activity_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  action AS action,
  option AS option,
  path AS path,
  NULL AS url,
  'activity_log' AS source_table
FROM activity_log
UNION ALL
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  action AS action,
  NULL AS option,
  NULL AS path,
  url AS url,
  'read_log' AS source_table
FROM read_log
UNION ALL
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  action AS action,
  NULL AS option,
  path AS path,
  NULL AS url,
  'form_log' AS source_table
FROM form_log
UNION ALL
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  NULL AS action,
  NULL AS option,
  NULL AS path,
  NULL AS url,
  'form_error_log' AS source_table
FROM form_error_log
UNION ALL
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  action AS action,
  NULL AS option,
  NULL AS path,
  NULL AS url,
  'access_log' AS source_table
FROM access_log
UNION ALL
SELECT
  stamp AS stamp,
  session AS session,
  action AS action,
  NULL AS option,
  NULL AS path,
  NULL AS url,
  'action_log_with_ip' AS source_table
FROM action_log_with_ip
accepted.description: Unified session-level events by unioning activity_log, read_log, form_log, form_error_log, access_log and action_log_with_ip where available. Preserves source table via source_table and standardizes stamp, session, action/path/url fields to help analyze session behavior across logs. | Use for: session funnel analysis across different logs; count events per session irrespective of source; identify sessions with form errors or access events
